item.title: NBA Expansion News: Three Finalists Emerge In Potential Las Vegas Expansion Team
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images In 2004, the Charlotte Bobcats joined the NBA as an expansion team, adding a new market to the professional basketball world. While much has changed since then, the total number of teams has remained the same, driving up parity across the association. Now, the league is finally deep enough to add more expansion teams, and it has picked Las Vegas as the next location. According to Shams Charania, the league is on the verge of a major decision : choosing among four potential ownership groups. One such group involves Kenny Smith , a former NBA guard turned analyst. “The NBA is getting closer and closer to a decision and a ruling on the winning bid for the Las Vegas group,” reported Shams Charania on ESPN . “Sources tell me all three finalists are at $10 billion, and potentially more. The three finalists are as follows: it’s the Walton family, it’s Bill Foley, owner of the Las Vegas Knights, as well as Jerry Collenagelo, who’s a basketball Hall of Famer. The Third group is headed by Steve Apolostoloipolis. He’s out of Canada, a billionaire, the former Bucks co-owner, and Kenny Smith.” Smith, 61, is best known for his time with the Houston Rockets in the 90s, when he averaged 12.6 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 5.3 assists per game on 49.0% shooting from the field. Smith was only a role player during his NBA tenure, but he could be a part owner of the next expansion team if his group’s bid wins the sweepstakes. “The process is much longer than I thought it would be, and being a part of it, it’s a great deal of education. I was blessed to be able to put a group together individually to raise a lot of capital to bring a part of Steve’s group and Mark’s group,” said Smith. “And so that’s where we are, and we’ll see what happens. It’s right down to the wire, and I haven’t lost a lot in the playoffs when it gets down to the wire.” The NBA has been building toward expansion for years , with multiple cities in discussion, including Mexico City and Vancouver. In the end, however, the league settled on Las Vegas, where the NBA has hosted various events over the years. Somehow, the city went until 2017 without its own professional team, but that changed with the formation of the NHL’s Golden Knights, the WNBA’s Aces, and the relocation of the NFL’s Raiders. The NBA is the last major sports league to add a team to Vegas, and it’s still a work in progress . After approving expansion, the league is still deciding who will run the ball club, and all the bids have crossed $10 billion. For NBA legend Kenny Smith, the status of his group’s bid is still unclear, but there’s no doubt he feels confident about his current position. As a two-time NBA champion during his playing days, Smith knows what it takes to succeed, and he’s ready to build something special in Vegas. What happens next, however, is entirely out of his hands, and it could very well determine the Western Conference hierarchy for several years to come.

Here’s everything you need to know about the saga that has erupted this week and the very famous name circulated as the possible successor to the (for now) current USMNT manager, Mauricio Pochettino. Who Is Pep Guardiola? Basically, Guardiola is the world’s gold standard for soccer management at the international club level, but someone whose experience has come primarily from coaching the world’s biggest stars. The best North American parallels might be pro baseball’s Tony La Russa, pro basketball’s Phil Jackson, college basketball’s Rick Pitino or college football’s Nick Saban. In other words, guys who have achieved the highest heights at multiple stops. Guardiola has won prolifically at three stops; FC Barcelona, Bayern Munich and most recently Manchester City. In total, the Spaniard owns 12 league titles, three UEFA Champions League crowns and four FIFA Club World Cups (in the now-defunct annual format). Why Does The USMNT Need A New Manager? Essentially, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is leaving to take over at Manchester United. Pochettino signed a four-year extension with U.S. Soccer to stay with the USMNT in August. But such is his stature that his name is often bandied about when a high-profile English or European job comes open. This time the rumors have real legs, though. ESPN’s Mark Ogden first reported Manchester United preferred Pochettino as a candidate to replace current manager Michael Carrick , and the Guardian’s Pablo Maurer and Jamie Jackson first confirmed the interest was mutual . Additional reports have negotiations progressing. The good news for U.S. fans is it appears U.S. Soccer will be compensated should Pochettino leave, with a $10 million buyout clause reportedly a part of his new contract. item.title: Mizzou volleyball adds three-player class on National Signing Day
item.description: Dawn Sullivan’s 2027 recruiting class features a nationally recognized setter, an accomplished defensive specialist and a St. Louis middle blocker. Mizzou announced the signings of Lucky Fasavalu, Dani Lewis and Marlee Steiner on Wednesday, adding three players who bring experience at the national, state and club levels. The group addresses three different positions for Sullivan’s program, with Fasavalu expected to help direct the offense, Lewis strengthening the back row and Steiner providing another option at the net. Fasavalu, a 5-foot-8 setter from Sierra Canyon High School in California, arrives in Columbia with an extensive list of individual accomplishments. She was named a MaxPreps First Team All-American in 2025 and earned recognition on the organization’s National Player of the Year watchlist. Fasavalu recently reached another milestone, recording her 2,000th career assist during Sierra Canyon’s postseason run. The Trailblazers advanced to the CIF Southern Section Division I championship match Nov. 7, finishing as runner-up to Mater Dei. Lewis, a 5-foot-5 defensive specialist from Lake Norman Charter in North Carolina, joins the Tigers after winning back-to-back state championships. The libero was named the most valuable player of North Carolina’s 4A state competition during the latest championship run. She also earned Charlotte-area Player of the Year recognition from the Charlotte Observer and played club volleyball with Carolina Union. Lewis served as a team captain at Lake Norman Charter, which finished the 2026 season with a 30-1 record. Steiner gives Missouri another in-state addition. The 6-foot-5 middle blocker from Lindbergh High School in St. Louis has experience competing with USA Volleyball’s national development programs and was selected to the U19 National Team roster. She also played club volleyball with High Performance STL. Steiner earned First Team All-State recognition in Missouri in 2025 and was named to the JVA All-National Team in each of the past two seasons. The three signings give Sullivan another recruiting group as Missouri continues building its roster for the future. With a setter who has surpassed 2,000 career assists, a defensive specialist with championship experience and a 6-foot-5 middle blocker, the Tigers bring in players with different skill sets and competitive backgrounds. Fasavalu, Lewis and Steiner are expected to join Missouri for the 2027 season.

item.title: Oregon's Dan Lanning calls out Michigan football for bad spending habits
item.description: Oregon's Dan Lanning calls out Michigan football for bad spending habits originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning took a slight shot at Michigan for how the football program has distributed its money. This came in response to comments about the Ducks' financial advantages in recruiting and roster building. The exchange began when Michigan Wolverines coach Kyle Whittingham suggested Oregon's reported $50 million budget gave the program a significant advantage in the increasingly competitive NIL landscape. Whittingham praised Lanning for his work, but also acknowledged the resources available to Oregon, mostly tied to Nike. "It doesn't hurt that you have $50-plus million dollars at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody,' Whittingham said. "Not everybody, but a lot of people." Lanning took issue with the basis of the comment. He responded by talking about Michigan's financial commitments, particularly money still owed to departing coaches. "They're spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players,'" Lanning said. He also suggested Michigan had secured players Oregon could not match financially. "I know they've signed a couple of guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do,' Lanning said. "Maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player." Dan Lanning’s response to Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham’s comments on Oregon being able to “outbid everybody” for recruits. pic.twitter.com/zsVwvrppUc — Ryan Clarke (@RyanTClarke) November 11, 2026 The comments add another storyline ahead of Michigan's trip to Eugene this week. Lanning and Whittingham know each other extremely well, being in the Pac-12 for their respective schools. Whittingham made the transition to Ann Arbor from Utah over the offseason. According to On3, Oregon quarterback Dante Moore carries a $5 million NIL valuation, ranking fourth nationally. EDGE Matayo Uiagalelei and safety Koi Perich also appear in the top 100, each valued at $2 million. Michigan has two players on the list. Quarterback Bryce Underwood carries a $3 million valuation, ranking 33rd. But in reality, his NIL deal with the school was a reported $12.5 million. EDGE John Henry Daley is valued at $2 million after coming over from Utah. Despite the back-and-forth, Lanning made it clear he respects Whittingham, calling him an unbelievable Hall of Fame-caliber coach. Both programs compete for top talent. However, this year hasn't been typical for either the Wolverines or Ducks. No. 18 Oregon hosts Michigan on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on FS1. item.title: Jacob Misiorowski wins unanimous NL Cy Young Award; Cam Schlittler claims AL honors
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Jacob Misiorowski #32 of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the third year in a row, the Cy Young race was somewhat of a foregone conclusion. Today, Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski was named the unanimous National League Cy Young Award winner, joining Randy Johnson (2001) and Justin Verlander (2022) as the only pitchers since 2000 to win the Cy Young and the World Series in the same year. He is the fourth Brewer to win the award in franchise history, following Rollie Fingers (1981), Pete Vuckovich (1982), and Corbin Burnes (2021). Misiorowski flashed as a rookie last year, starting off hot and (controversially) making the All-Star team after just five career starts, but he struggled with his command down the stretch and finished the year with a 4.36 ERA. This year, in his first full season as a big-leaguer, Misiorowski worked out the kinks and became completely and utterly dominant, leading the majors in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), and WHIP (0.80) while going 16-5. Highlights from his record-breaking season include: Making history with the first-ever 15-strikeout “Maddux” (a complete-game shutout on fewer than 100 pitches) in an early-June game against the Phillies. Misiorowski was a Kyle Schwarber single away from a perfect game, and his 15 strikeouts tied Corbin Burnes for the second-most in a game in Brewers history, behind only Ben Sheets (18). Setting the record for the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starting pitcher, a 105.5-mph fastball. Throwing 1,115 pitches at 100 mph or harder, the most in a season since tracking began in 2008, shattering Jordan Hicks’ previous record of 673 in 2018. Making the National League All-Star team for the second time in as many years. Holding opponents to a .157 batting average, the lowest on record for a full season. Becoming the first Brewer in history to lead the league in both ERA and strikeouts in the same season. Starting the game that clinched the first World Series title in franchise history. Cristopher Sánchez of the Phillies finished second for the second year in a row, receiving 17 of 30 second-place votes, while Braves left-hander Chris Sale finished third. In the American League, fellow second-year starter Cam Schlittler also won the award unanimously. Schlittler put together an amazing season of his own, leading AL starters in WAR (7.0), ERA (1.95), and ERA+ (215). Dylan Cease of the Blue Jays finished second, and rookie Parker Messick of the Guardians finished third.

item.title: What makes a reliever of the year?
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - MARCH 16: Alex Vesia (L) #51 and Tanner Scott #66 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walk on the field prior to a Spring Training game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Camelback Ranch on March 16, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images LOS ANGELES — The Baseball Writers Association of America added a new award this season, honoring the top relief pitcher in each league each year. The inaugural winner of the National League Reliever of the Year is Mason Miller in a landslide. The San Diego Padres closer received all 30 first-place votes. His stats tell the story, as Miller put up a 1.67 ERA, best among all National League pitchers with 50 innings. Miller was also tops in xERA (1.70), FIP (1.17), xFIP (1.54), strikeout rate (an eye-popping 47.4 percent), strikeout-minus-walk rate (37.9 percent), and saves (38, in 41 attempts). I had a vote in this award this year, and I voted Miller in the top spot. Before casting my ballot, I asked a few Dodgers relievers how they might define relief pitcher of the year, and in the course of our conversations, Miller also gained their respect, too. “It’s got to be Mason Miller,” said left-hander Alex Veisa. “He has been unbelievable to watch. His stuff is — you know, when he was in Oakland, right, it’s like how could someone get any better? And he’s still getting better.” “It will probably be limited to a closer role, and in the National League for closers, how can you not say Mason Miller?” asked southpaw Jack Dreyer. I was not only certain pretty early on about Miller in the top spot, but also Johan Duran of the Philadelphia Phillies seemed like the clear choice for my No. 2 on the ballot. Duran saved 33 games in 35 tries, all while finishing second to Miller among NL relievers in ERA (1.82), xERA (2.04), FIP (1.41), xFIP (1.74), and strikeout-minus-walk rate (31.4 percent). “Someone that contributes to a winning baseball team and the biggest moments, he gets outs there frequently,” said right-hander Evan Phillips. “It’s interesting to point out a couple guys down there in San Diego that have been used a ton this year — Mason Miller and Adrián Morejón. item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - APRIL 17: Eduardo Rodriguez #57 of the Arizona Diamondbacks looks on following the first inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on April 17, 2025 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Unsurprisingly, Jacob Misiorowski was the winner of the NL Cy Young award, getting all thirty first-place votes. But there was some love for Arizona further down the ballot, with Eduardo Rodriguez getting two fifth-place votes, from Tyler Kepner of the Athletic, and Dejan Kovacevic of DK Pittsburgh Sports. E-Rod is the first D-back to be mentioned since 2023, and the first apart from Zac Gallen since 2018. Rodriguez did considerably better in the old school metrics. His ERA of 2.89 was fifth among qualified pitchers in the National League, and by wins (16), he only trailed Cristopher Sánchez of the Phillies (18). Innings pitched also had E-Rod ranked highly, third in the NL. [Though in a sign of the times, only two pitchers reached even 190 innings. As recently as 2014, twenty-seven pitchers in the NL did] But Rodriguez ranked only seventh by bWAR among pitchers (4.7), and fWAR ranked him all the way down at 12th, on 3.2 wins, likely due to his FIP being a run more than his ERA. In the old-school era – like when Brandon Webb lost out on Rookie of the Year in 2003 to Dontrelle Willis, I suspect Eduardo would perhaps have made the top three. But W’s and, to a lesser extent, ERA are no longer seen as the definitive measure of pitcher quality. I’m somewhat torn about that. Wins, I get. While good starters will tend to pick up more of them, the offense plays a huge part in that, and is something over which the pitcher has no control. ERA is also dependent on external factors, albeit to a lesser extent, with defense a factor, beyond what is recorded in earned vs. unearned runs. But generating weak contact, leading to “better” defense, feels like a skill too. Still, there’s no denying Rodriguez had an excellent, and much-needed, season for Arizona. item.title: Former First-Round Pick Could Give Detroit Red Wings Major Trade Opportunity
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have plenty of questions to answer about their future, and an intriguing trade opportunity could be developing in Washington. Former first-round pick Ivan Miroshnichenko is looking for a fresh start, and Detroit could be an interesting destination for the talented 22-year-old forward. According to Kyle Morton of Daily Faceoff , Miroshnichenko’s agent, Dan Milstein, has received permission from the Capitals to help facilitate a trade. The goal is to find a team willing to give the young winger a more significant opportunity than he currently has in Washington. There is no confirmed report that the Red Wings have contacted the Capitals or expressed interest in Miroshnichenko. However, with interim general manager Shawn Horcoff evaluating Detroit’s long-term direction, the former No. 20 overall pick could be worth considering. Apr 14, 2026; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Washington Capitals left wing Ivan Miroshnichenko (63) wrists a shot on goal as Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Ivan Provorov (9) defends during the third period at Nationwide Arena. Mandatory Credit: Russell LaBounty-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Capitals Forward Ivan Miroshnichenko Looking for Fresh Start Miroshnichenko was selected 20th overall by Washington in the 2022 NHL Draft, but establishing himself as a regular NHL contributor has been difficult. Despite possessing considerable offensive upside, he has struggled to secure consistent playing time in the Capitals’ crowded forward group. item.title: Youngest pair of Cy Young winners in 41 years shows future of pitching has arrived
item.description: They embraced the modern ethos of pitching from the moment they turned professional. And now Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler have proven the future of pitching has arrived. Misiorowski, 24, and Schlittler, 25, won the National and American league Cy Young Awards , respectively, in balloting announced on Nov. 11. And in doing so, they made a certain kind of history: They are the youngest Cy Young-winning duo since 1985, when 20-year-old Dwight Gooden and 21-year-old Bret Saberhagen took home NL and AL honors. Gooden and Saberhagen went on to excellent, World Series-winning careers, even if they could not sustain that level of dominance when they were barely or not quite old enough to legally drink. And their victories didn’t necessarily portend a changing of the guard in the pitching pantheon. Yet, The Miz and Schlitt seemed to prove a point in making 30 and 33 starts and consistently pitching deep into games for the Milwaukee Brewers and New York Yankees , respectively: Yes, significant gains in velocity can be taught – and throwing as hard as you can as long as you can, at least for one season, is sustainable. Schlittler’s fastball barely hit 88 mph coming out of Northeastern as a seventh-round pick in 2022. Misiorowski was in that same range when Brewers scouts pondered drafting him out of high school. Yet both young men matured physically. Schlittler now packs 215 pounds on his 6-foot-6 frame, while Misiorowski is still a relative drink of water at 6-7, 201 – but seemingly growing every day. Perhaps more important, they got drafted by clubs that were fantastic fits. Schlittler’s mechanics and repertoire were remade under a pitching department led by Sam Briend, a former Driveline director of pitching and now the senior voice among Yankee pitching staffers. One of Briend’s first hires, Preston Claiborne, came up the ladder with Schlittler and is now assistant pitching coach for the major league club. Meanwhile, Misiorowski has exceeded the hopes Brewers scouts held when they projected he’d eventually top 100 mph. Try 105 mph. The Miz threw 28 of the 35 hardest pitches in the major leagues this season, ranging from 104 to 105.5 mph. That’s great eye candy, but the numbers at the end of September are even better: 252 strikeouts with a 1.80 ERA, two of the seven major statistical categories in which Misiorowski led the major leagues. Schlittler won his own ERA title, posting a 1.95 mark to lead the AL. And he pitched 193 2/3 innings, just shy of the 200-inning plateau that was once the bare minimum of quality production, yet just three pitchers exceeded this season. Still, for Schlittler to reach that mark in his first full season is an excellent sign he might yet resemble what we all considered an ace. item.title: Mount Olive volleyball tops North Hunterdon, advances to Group final
item.description: MOUNT OLIVE — Ava Diaz held the NJSIAA Group 3 North volleyball trophy tightly, with both arms. Amidst the chaotic back gym, the Mount Olive senior libero looked back on the season – and a chance to make history. The Marauders held off North Hunterdon, 25-18, 25-23, 25-23, to clinch the sectional title and extend a confusing and challenging season. Diaz played libero for Mount Olive for the first time, just her second year at the defensive spot. But the big change impacted outside hitters Izabella Osoria and Olivia Drucks. Instead of just stepping up at the net, both became setters – usually to each other. What head coach "modified 6-2" was the brainchild of assistant coach Lee Clowers back in preseason. It took a little while to adjust – noted in the Marauders' lone loss at Randolph on Sept. 9 – but it's become their not-so-secret weapon. David Morgan Morgan went undrafted in 2022 but was invited to a workout with other prospects at Petco Park. The California native impressed the scouts and signed with the club ahead of the 2022 season. When Morgan made his MLB debut with the Padres in 2025, he was electric. In 47 1/3 innings of work, the right-hander quickly became a high-leverage option for San Diego down the stretch, authoring a 2.66 ERA in that time. Overall Grade: C Last season was a step back from that dominant rookie campaign. Morgan posted a 3.78 ERA, 1.77 WHIP and .282 opponent batting average across 33 1/3 innings. Those aren’t horrible numbers, but they aren’t great either. In 2025, Morgan was one of the best rookie pitchers in baseball. That wasn’t the case in his sophomore season. That wasn’t entirely his fault. Morgan landed on the injured list with left knee inflammation right before the Trade Deadline. He missed 38 games before undergoing a rehab assignment in Triple-A. After returning, he dominated. Morgan pitched to a 2.92 ERA in his final 15 appearances and a 1.17 ERA in his last seven outings. Overall, it wasn’t a bad season from the 27-year-old. The sixth-youngest pitcher to win the award, the 24-year-old Misiorowski ran away from the competition over the final four months of the season.
